newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Chances of INL buying into Sky only 50-50.
newsitem.headline: Chances of INL buying into Sky only 50-50.

text.p: The chances of New Zealand's Independent Newspapers Ltd buying into pay-TV operator Sky Network Television are only 50-50, INL Mmanaging director Mike Robson said on Monday.
"It's not a done deal," Robson told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"We've always said that everything has to be correct for us to go ahead, and in the event that occurs we will. If it doesn't, we would regretfully have to walk away. But we're not at either stage at the moment," he said.
Robson added: "It's always been a 50-50 thing, and that's where it sits at the moment."
INL was widely expected to announce it had secured in excess of 80 percent of Sky TV when it reported its first-half profit result earlier on Monday.
But INL said difficult issues relating to Sky's shareholding structure had to be resolved if the investment were to go ahead.
"All of the various ingredients in the deal have to be perfectly right in the deal or we won't do it," Robson said.
"Unless we get what we want, we won't be doing it."
In October last year INL said it was negotiating with a group of companies that together own more than 80 percent of Sky to buy a substantial stake.

Those companies include Heatley Jarvis Investments (15.8 percent), Todd Corporation (8.8 percent), Tappenden Construction (7.7 percent) and United States-based HKP Partners (51.1 percent). HKP is partly owned by Bell Atlantic and Ameritech, which in turn own half of Telecom Corp of New Zealand.
State-owned Television New Zealand holds the remaining 16.4 percent of Sky and media reports say it wants to raise its stake to about 25 percent.
But Robson said it was not fair to assume that TVNZ was the stumbling block to INL sealing the Sky deal.
"No that's not fair at all. It's not any one ingredient, it's a complex deal and unless we have everything in place, we're not going to sign, so that's where it's at," he said.
Robson was hopeful that the deal would go ahead, but indicated it may be some time yet before a final decision was made.

"We thought that we'd get through the issues reasonably quickly, but we haven't, and seeing it's taken a long while to get where we are, it may take us even further if we are going to be successful -- I wouldn't like to put a time frame on it.
INL is just under half-owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation. Sky is not related to Murdoch's 40 percent-owned European-based satellite network BSkyB.
